transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the production plan for the next window. We need to cover 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives. I'm aware we currently have only 450 power modules released for use, with additional units sitting in quality-hold. Before I make any allocation decisions, I need each of you to give me your input: process engineering on any constraints, quality on the status of those held modules, logistics on shipment readiness, and product compliance on any open items. Once I have that full picture, I'll issue a complete disposition for every scheduled order.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from my engineering BOM review. Each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module. I completed this review after the latest engineering change but haven't yet entered the revised quantities in the planning system, so the system may not reflect the correct requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've completed an inspection of the quality-hold area. Exactly 150 of the held modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing. I documented this in a local inspection worksheet, but it hasn't been attached to the material record yet, so it wouldn't show up in the system. If we proceed with the bake and testing, those 150 modules could be added to the released pool, bringing the total to 600 power modules.

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. From a logistics perspective, I have customer shipment confirmations that are relevant to the production plan. I need to share the specific shipment timing requirements with the group so they can factor into your disposition.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance requirement from my destination review. Every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment. I completed this review for the export destination but have not yet added the requirement to the dispatch checklist, so it wouldn't currently appear in our standard shipment documentation. This means that for any Model Y drives we plan to ship, we need to ensure these traceability and certification requirements are built into the production and shipment disposition.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: Thank you all for your input. Let me summarize what I now have before making my disposition. Ravi, you've confirmed that each Model X requires 2 power modules and each Model Y requires 1, meaning the full plan of 240 Model X and 120 Model Y would require 600 power modules total. Mara, you've confirmed that 150 of the held modules can be recovered via a 6-hour controlled bake and insulation testing, which would bring our released pool from 450 to 600 — exactly enough to cover the full plan. Simone, you've flagged that every Model Y drive needs serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment, and this must be built into the disposition. Jon, I still need to hear the specific shipment timing requirements from logistics before I can finalize the disposition. Could you please share those details now?
